3.  The FIR in question was lodged under Section 498A, 354, 506, 376, 323, 504, 494, 109 & 120B IPC by the informant who is wife of the present applicant.

1 are on the face is bald and scandalous.
The FIR reveals that the victim was married to the applicant in the year 2013 and reached matrimonial home in the year 2016.
In the year 2018, a girl child was born.
It is stated that thereafter, the entire matrimonial family used to misbehave with her.
Scandalous allegations have been levelled against father-in-law of having inappropriately touched her and committed wrong on her.
Bald allegations were levelled against mother-in-law also.
She also stated that when the child was unwell, none of the matrimonial family members spent money for her treatment.
She also made allegations against her own brother-in-law of inappropriately behaving with her.
Allegations went on to say that jewellery was also snatched by the entire matrimonial family.
It was also stated that the applicant had married again.
4. The FIR version clearly demonstrates that a law which was framed for protection of women is being rampantly used as a tool for oppression.

It also transpires from record that the other matrimonial family members had approached this Court by filing Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.4496 of 2024 in which they were granted interim protection vide order dated 26.06.2024.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.4496 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant, who is in custody since 02.07.2024, has been arrested based upon scandalous and bald allegations without there being any material to corroborate.
5. This Court cannot shut its eye to the blatant misuse of a law which was framed/enacted for protecting the women, and the present case demonstrates that it has been used as a tool for oppression.

6. Considering the aforesaid facts coupled with the fact that there is no material whatsoever to substantiate the allegation against the applicant and even otherwise, the offence under Section 376 IPC is not made out against the applicant in view of Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC, a clear case for bail is made out.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Kausal Tiwari be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with one surety of Rs.5,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
